meta: Listening, talking, watching, making video: where do AI's senses live? The old way glued separate machines together and lost information like a game of telephone · the new way puts text, images and sound into one brain.
prompt: What can I cook for 3 people in 20 minutes?

muc.title: Where do the senses live?
muc.text: Last time, AI made a video from one sentence. Listen, talk, watch, make. So where do those senses live inside AI?

muc.title: Many separate machines glued together
muc.text: The old way glued many machines together: one turns voice into text, one describes pictures in text, then everything goes to the machine that reads text. With each handoff, information gets lost, like a game of telephone.

muc.title: Everything becomes small pieces
muc.text: The new way: everything is cut into small pieces called tokens, like in the video about tokens. Text becomes pieces, pictures become little squares, sound becomes short clips. It all goes into one brain.

muc.title: It gets both tone and picture
muc.text: Hearing sound directly, it can pick up tone: whether "fine, whatever" is said happily or sulkily. Seeing a picture directly, it can read charts and see where you're pointing.

muc.title: Send one message: a photo plus your voice
muc.text: Take a photo of your fridge and send it to AI, then record: "What can I cook for 3 people in 20 minutes?" See what it suggests from exactly what you have.

muc.title: Many senses, still can be wrong
muc.text: But many senses doesn't mean no mistakes. For important things, you're still the one who checks.

muc.title: Three series in one picture
muc.text: Looking back: AI learns by turning billions of knobs itself. It's graded by tests, arenas and your own test. And now it listens, talks, watches and makes, all in one brain.

muc.title: Thanks for coming along
muc.text: Thank you for coming along for all 18 parts. Just got here? Go back to part 1, "How AI learns".
